newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-DUVILLARD SHINES IN DOWNHILL PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-DUVILLARD SHINES IN DOWNHILL PRACTICE.

text.p: Frenchman Adrien Duvillard hinted he was back at his brilliant best by clocking the fastest time on Thursday during the second practice for Saturday's men's World Cup downhill.
Duvillard, who wonfame by winning a World Cup downhill in 1993 in Lillehammer, Norway, but has since seen his career upset by a string of injuries, left his nearest rival over one second behind.

Nobody could match Duvillard's best time of two minutes 3.95 seconds, not even compatriot Luc Alphand, the downhill World Cup leader, who had to be the content with the second fastest time of 2:05.14.
Little-known Slovenian Ales Brezavsek was third fastest in 2:05.31 in a session made tricky by strong winds and poor visibility.

The 27-year-old Duvillard, who shares Alphand's room on the circuit and uses the same skis, had suggested hard times were behind him by finishing fifth in a World Cup downhill last December in Val Gardena.

"It's good to be skiing well again," he said. "Of course, this was only practice but it will do my confidence a lot of good. I still have a bit of flu but it's getting better and I should be all right on Saturday."
But Alphand, who has already posted wins in Val Gardena and Bormio this season, warned he should still be regarded as the favourite for Saturday's race by saying he had a fairly cautious run.

"It was important not to get hurt," said the 31-year-old Frenchman, who set the fastest time in Wednesday's first practice. "This piste is not a very steep one but it's physically demanding because it's bumpy," he added.
A slalom on Sunday as well as the first combined event of the men's season will complete the weekend programme in Chamonix, a ski village overlooked by Mont Blanc.
